title: Boss: The bank
summary: Build a bank's domain model in four stages: invariants, account types, transaction records, and a bank that works through an interface.

steps.title: The brief
body: You are modelling a small bank. Money is the classic place where *almost right* is not good enough, so the types themselves must make wrong states impossible.
Four stages, each a fresh editor:
1. An account that protects its balance.
2. Account types that share a base class but disagree about withdrawals.
3. A transaction history built from records.
4. A bank that moves money between any accounts that fit an interface.
Throughout: `ArgumentException` means *bad value passed in*. `InvalidOperationException` means *the account cannot do that right now*.

steps.title: Stage 1: An account with invariants
prompt: Write a class `Account` whose balance can never be wrong.
- constructor `Account(string owner, decimal openingBalance)`: throws `ArgumentException` when the owner is empty or only spaces, or the opening balance is negative
- `Owner` (`string`): `get` only
- `Balance` (`decimal`): readable by anyone, settable only inside the class
- `void Deposit(decimal amount)`: throws `ArgumentException` when the amount is zero or negative
- `void Withdraw(decimal amount)`: throws `ArgumentException` when the amount is zero or negative, and `InvalidOperationException` when it is more than the balance
A refused call must leave the balance exactly as it was.
solution: public decimal Balance { get; private set; }
throw new ArgumentException("Opening balance cannot be negative");
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
template: var dojoA = new Account("Maya", 100m);
Dojo.Eq("Owner comes from the constructor", "Maya", dojoA.Owner);
Dojo.Eq("Balance starts at the opening balance", 100m, dojoA.Balance);
Dojo.Check("Owner cannot be set from outside", typeof(Account).GetProperty("Owner") is { } dojoOwner && dojoOwner.SetMethod?.IsPublic != true, "Owner should be a property with no public setter");
Dojo.Check("Balance cannot be set from outside", typeof(Account).GetProperty("Balance") is { } dojoBal && dojoBal.SetMethod?.IsPublic != true, "Balance should be a property with a private setter");
Dojo.Check("Account has no public fields", typeof(Account).GetFields().Length == 0, "Use properties or private fields");
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("an empty owner throws ArgumentException", () => new Account("", 10m));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("an owner of only spaces throws ArgumentException", () => new Account("  ", 10m));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a negative opening balance throws ArgumentException", () => new Account("Ben", -1m));
Dojo.Try("an opening balance of 0 is allowed", () => { Dojo.Eq("an opening balance of 0 is allowed", 0m, new Account("Ben", 0m).Balance); });
Dojo.Try("Deposit(50) raises Balance to 150", () => { dojoA.Deposit(50m); Dojo.Eq("Deposit(50) raises Balance to 150", 150m, dojoA.Balance); });
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("Deposit(0) throws ArgumentException", () => dojoA.Deposit(0m));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("Deposit(-20) throws ArgumentException", () => dojoA.Deposit(-20m));
Dojo.Try("Withdraw(30) lowers Balance to 120", () => { dojoA.Withdraw(30m); Dojo.Eq("Withdraw(30) lowers Balance to 120", 120m, dojoA.Balance); });
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("Withdraw(0) throws ArgumentException", () => dojoA.Withdraw(0m));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("Withdraw(120.01) throws InvalidOperationException", () => dojoA.Withdraw(120.01m));
Dojo.Eq("refused calls leave Balance at 120", 120m, dojoA.Balance);
Dojo.Try("Withdraw(120) can empty the account", () => { dojoA.Withdraw(120m); Dojo.Eq("Withdraw(120) can empty the account", 0m, dojoA.Balance); });
{{CODE}}
hints: The two properties are `public string Owner { get; }` and `public decimal Balance { get; private set; }`.
Every method starts with its guards: `if (...) throw new ArgumentException("...");`. Guards come before any change to `Balance`.
`string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(owner)` catches both the empty name and the name made of spaces. In `Withdraw`, check `amount <= 0` first, then `amount > Balance`.

steps.title: Stage 2: Account types
prompt: The bank now offers two kinds of account. They share almost everything, but disagree on one question: *may this amount be withdrawn?*
The starter gives you an `Account` base class. Finish the model.
**`Account`**
- make it `abstract`
- add `abstract bool CanWithdraw(decimal amount)`
- `Withdraw` must throw `InvalidOperationException` when `CanWithdraw` says no
**`CurrentAccount : Account`**
- constructor `CurrentAccount(string owner, decimal overdraftLimit)`
- `OverdraftLimit` (`decimal`, `get` only)
- may go below zero, but never further than the overdraft limit. With a limit of 100 and a balance of 50, withdrawing 150 is allowed and 150.01 is not.
**`SavingsAccount : Account`** (sealed)
- constructor `SavingsAccount(string owner, decimal interestRate)`
- may never go below zero
- `void AddInterest()` adds `Balance * interestRate` to the balance. A rate of `0.10m` turns 200 into 220.
starter: public decimal Balance { get; protected set; }
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
// ask CanWithdraw before taking the money
solution: public decimal Balance { get; protected set; }
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
public CurrentAccount(string owner, decimal overdraftLimit) : base(owner)
public SavingsAccount(string owner, decimal interestRate) : base(owner)
template: Dojo.Check("Account is abstract", typeof(Account).IsAbstract, "Declare it as: abstract class Account");
Dojo.Check("CurrentAccount inherits from Account", typeof(CurrentAccount).BaseType == typeof(Account), "class CurrentAccount : Account");
Dojo.Check("SavingsAccount inherits from Account and is sealed", typeof(SavingsAccount).BaseType == typeof(Account) && typeof(SavingsAccount).IsSealed, "sealed class SavingsAccount : Account");
var dojoCur = new CurrentAccount("Maya", 100m);
Dojo.Eq("CurrentAccount keeps Owner from the base class", "Maya", dojoCur.Owner);
Dojo.Eq("OverdraftLimit is stored", 100m, dojoCur.OverdraftLimit);
dojoCur.Deposit(50m);
Dojo.Eq("current: CanWithdraw(150) with balance 50 and limit 100", true, dojoCur.CanWithdraw(150m));
Dojo.Eq("current: CanWithdraw(150.01) is false", false, dojoCur.CanWithdraw(150.01m));
Dojo.Try("current: Withdraw(120) takes the balance to -70", () => { dojoCur.Withdraw(120m); Dojo.Eq("current: Withdraw(120) takes the balance to -70", -70m, dojoCur.Balance); });
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("current: Withdraw(31) past the overdraft throws InvalidOperationException", () => dojoCur.Withdraw(31m));
Dojo.Eq("current: the refused withdrawal changed nothing", -70m, dojoCur.Balance);
var dojoSav = new SavingsAccount("Ben", 0.10m);
dojoSav.Deposit(200m);
Dojo.Eq("savings: CanWithdraw(200) is true", true, dojoSav.CanWithdraw(200m));
Dojo.Eq("savings: CanWithdraw(200.01) is false", false, dojoSav.CanWithdraw(200.01m));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("savings: Withdraw(500) throws InvalidOperationException", () => dojoSav.Withdraw(500m));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("savings: Withdraw(-5) still throws ArgumentException", () => dojoSav.Withdraw(-5m));
Dojo.Try("savings: AddInterest() at 10% turns 200 into 220", () => { dojoSav.AddInterest(); Dojo.Eq("savings: AddInterest() at 10% turns 200 into 220", 220m, dojoSav.Balance); });
Account[] dojoAll = { dojoCur, dojoSav };
var dojoAnswers = new List<bool>();
foreach (Account dojoAcc in dojoAll) dojoAnswers.Add(dojoAcc.CanWithdraw(25m));
Dojo.Eq("through an Account[], each type answers CanWithdraw(25) its own way", new List<bool> { true, true }, dojoAnswers);
foreach (Account dojoAcc in dojoAll) dojoAnswers.Add(dojoAcc.CanWithdraw(225m));
Dojo.Eq("...and CanWithdraw(225) is false for both", new List<bool> { true, true, false, false }, dojoAnswers);
{{CODE}}
hints: In the base: add `abstract` to the class, add `public abstract bool CanWithdraw(decimal amount);`, and in `Withdraw` put `if (!CanWithdraw(amount)) throw new InvalidOperationException("...");` before the subtraction.
Each derived class passes the owner up with `: base(owner)` and supplies `public override bool CanWithdraw(decimal amount)`.
Current: `return Balance - amount >= -OverdraftLimit;`. Savings: `return amount <= Balance;`. `AddInterest` can set `Balance` directly because the setter is `protected`.

steps.title: Stage 3: Transaction records
prompt: A bank must be able to say what happened. Give the account a history made of records.
Add to the starter:
- an enum `TransactionType` with `Deposit` and `Withdrawal`
- a record `Transaction` with `Type` (`TransactionType`), `Amount` (`decimal`) and `BalanceAfter` (`decimal`), in that order
- in `Account`, a property `History` of type `IReadOnlyList<Transaction>`
Every successful deposit and withdrawal adds one transaction to the end of the history. A refused call adds nothing.

> **Tip:** `IReadOnlyList<Transaction>` is an interface that `List<Transaction>` already implements. Keep a private list, and expose it through a property of the interface type. Callers can read and count, but they get no `Add`.
starter: public decimal Balance { get; private set; }
// a private list of transactions, and a public read-only History
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
solution: record Transaction(TransactionType Type, decimal Amount, decimal BalanceAfter);
public decimal Balance { get; private set; }
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
template: Dojo.Check("TransactionType is an enum", typeof(TransactionType).IsEnum, "Declare it with the enum keyword");
Dojo.Check("Transaction is a record", typeof(Transaction).GetMethod("<Clone>$") != null, "Declare it with the record keyword");
Dojo.Eq("two transactions with the same data are equal", true, new Transaction(TransactionType.Deposit, 5m, 5m) == new Transaction(TransactionType.Deposit, 5m, 5m));
var dojoA = new Account();
IReadOnlyList<Transaction> dojoH = dojoA.History;
Dojo.Eq("History starts empty", 0, dojoH.Count);
dojoA.Deposit(100m);
dojoA.Withdraw(30m);
dojoA.Deposit(5m);
Dojo.Eq("three successful operations make three transactions", 3, dojoA.History.Count);
Dojo.Try("the first is Deposit 100, balance 100", () => Dojo.Eq("the first is Deposit 100, balance 100", new Transaction(TransactionType.Deposit, 100m, 100m), dojoA.History[0]));
Dojo.Try("the second is Withdrawal 30, balance 70", () => Dojo.Eq("the second is Withdrawal 30, balance 70", new Transaction(TransactionType.Withdrawal, 30m, 70m), dojoA.History[1]));
Dojo.Try("the third is Deposit 5, balance 75", () => Dojo.Eq("the third is Deposit 5, balance 75", new Transaction(TransactionType.Deposit, 5m, 75m), dojoA.History[2]));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("Withdraw(999) still throws InvalidOperationException", () => dojoA.Withdraw(999m));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("Deposit(0) still throws ArgumentException", () => dojoA.Deposit(0m));
Dojo.Eq("refused calls add nothing to History", 3, dojoA.History.Count);
Dojo.Eq("a second account has its own History", 0, new Account().History.Count);
Dojo.Check("Account has no public fields", typeof(Account).GetFields().Length == 0, "Keep the list private");
{{CODE}}
hints: The two new types are one line each: `enum TransactionType { Deposit, Withdrawal }` and `record Transaction(TransactionType Type, decimal Amount, decimal BalanceAfter);`
Inside `Account`: `private readonly List<Transaction> _history = new List<Transaction>();` and `public IReadOnlyList<Transaction> History => _history;`
Add to the history **after** changing `Balance`, at the very end of each method, so the guards have already run: `_history.Add(new Transaction(TransactionType.Deposit, amount, Balance));`

steps.title: Stage 4: A bank that works through an interface
prompt: Last stage. The bank moves money between accounts, and it must work with **any** account type, including ones the tests bring along. So it depends on an interface.
**`IAccount`** is given in the starter.
**`BasicAccount : IAccount`**
- constructor `BasicAccount(string owner, decimal openingBalance)`
- `CanWithdraw` is `true` when the amount is positive and no more than the balance
- `Deposit` throws `ArgumentException` for zero or negative amounts
- `Withdraw` throws `InvalidOperationException` when `CanWithdraw` is `false`
**`Bank`**
- `void Open(IAccount account)` adds an account. Owners are unique.
- `int Count`: how many accounts are open
- `decimal TotalBalance`: the sum of all balances

- `bool Transfer(string fromOwner, string toOwner, decimal amount)` moves the money and returns `true`. It returns `false` and moves **nothing** when either owner is unknown, or the source account says it cannot withdraw that amount.
`Bank` must never mention `BasicAccount`.
starter: public bool Transfer(string fromOwner, string toOwner, decimal amount)
solution: public decimal Balance { get; private set; }
throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
throw new InvalidOperationException("Cannot withdraw that amount");
private readonly Dictionary<string, IAccount> _accounts = new Dictionary<string, IAccount>();
public bool Transfer(string fromOwner, string toOwner, decimal amount)
template: IAccount dojoMaya = new BasicAccount("Maya", 100m);
IAccount dojoBen = new BasicAccount("Ben", 20m);
Dojo.Eq("BasicAccount stores Owner", "Maya", dojoMaya.Owner);
Dojo.Eq("BasicAccount stores the opening Balance", 100m, dojoMaya.Balance);
Dojo.Eq("CanWithdraw(100) is true with a balance of 100", true, dojoMaya.CanWithdraw(100m));
Dojo.Eq("CanWithdraw(100.01) is false", false, dojoMaya.CanWithdraw(100.01m));
Dojo.Eq("CanWithdraw(0) is false", false, dojoMaya.CanWithdraw(0m));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("Withdraw(500) throws InvalidOperationException", () => dojoMaya.Withdraw(500m));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("Deposit(-1) throws ArgumentException", () => dojoMaya.Deposit(-1m));

Dojo.Check("BasicAccount.Balance cannot be set from outside", typeof(BasicAccount).GetProperty("Balance") is { } dojoBal && dojoBal.SetMethod?.IsPublic != true, "Use: public decimal Balance { get; private set; }");
var dojoBank = new Bank();
Dojo.Eq("a new Bank has Count 0", 0, dojoBank.Count);
Dojo.Eq("a new Bank has TotalBalance 0", 0m, dojoBank.TotalBalance);
dojoBank.Open(dojoMaya);
dojoBank.Open(dojoBen);
var dojoIce = new DojoFrozenAccount("Cy", 500m);
dojoBank.Open(dojoIce);
Dojo.Eq("Count is 3 after opening three accounts", 3, dojoBank.Count);
Dojo.Eq("TotalBalance is 620", 620m, dojoBank.TotalBalance);
Dojo.Try("Transfer(Maya, Ben, 60) returns true", () => Dojo.Eq("Transfer(Maya, Ben, 60) returns true", true, dojoBank.Transfer("Maya", "Ben", 60m)));
Dojo.Eq("...Maya has 40", 40m, dojoMaya.Balance);
Dojo.Eq("...Ben has 80", 80m, dojoBen.Balance);
Dojo.Try("Transfer(Maya, Ben, 41) returns false: not enough money", () => Dojo.Eq("Transfer(Maya, Ben, 41) returns false: not enough money", false, dojoBank.Transfer("Maya", "Ben", 41m)));
Dojo.Try("Transfer from an unknown owner returns false", () => Dojo.Eq("Transfer from an unknown owner returns false", false, dojoBank.Transfer("Nobody", "Ben", 1m)));
Dojo.Try("Transfer to an unknown owner returns false", () => Dojo.Eq("Transfer to an unknown owner returns false", false, dojoBank.Transfer("Maya", "Nobody", 1m)));
Dojo.Eq("...and Maya still has 40", 40m, dojoMaya.Balance);

Dojo.Try("a frozen account (a type Bank has never seen) refuses to pay out", () => Dojo.Eq("a frozen account (a type Bank has never seen) refuses to pay out", false, dojoBank.Transfer("Cy", "Ben", 10m)));
Dojo.Try("...but it can receive money", () => Dojo.Eq("...but it can receive money", true, dojoBank.Transfer("Ben", "Cy", 30m)));
Dojo.Eq("...Cy now has 530", 530m, dojoIce.Balance);
Dojo.Eq("transfers never create or destroy money: TotalBalance is still 620", 620m, dojoBank.TotalBalance);
{{CODE}}
class DojoFrozenAccount : IAccount
public string Owner { get; }
public decimal Balance { get; private set; }
public DojoFrozenAccount(string owner, decimal balance) { Owner = owner; Balance = balance; }
public bool CanWithdraw(decimal amount) { return false; }
public void Deposit(decimal amount) { Balance += amount; }
public void Withdraw(decimal amount) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Account is frozen"); }
hints: `BasicAccount` is stage 1 again with `: IAccount` on the class line and a `CanWithdraw` method. Every interface member must be `public`.
In `Bank`, a `private readonly Dictionary<string, IAccount>` keyed by owner makes lookups easy: `ContainsKey(fromOwner)` answers *is this owner known?*. `TotalBalance` is a `foreach` over `.Values`.

`Transfer` asks three questions before touching any money: is `fromOwner` known, is `toOwner` known, and does `from.CanWithdraw(amount)` say yes? Only then `from.Withdraw(amount); to.Deposit(amount); return true;`
